comparator.name: Archaeology (Archeologie)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted 2026–27 OER for VU bachelor Archaeology, checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER confirms the exact normalized Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory alongside a separate English-language Archaeology trajectory. Its ordinary 180-EC curriculum is 60 EC of ten compulsory first-year courses; 78 EC of thirteen compulsory post-propaedeutic courses; a 12-EC bachelor thesis in the Dutch trajectory; and 30 EC genuinely free third-year academic profiling space. Field School 1 and 2, materials research, digital archaeology and excavation-to-publication work are prescribed in the ordinary curriculum. The English-track thesis is the same role in a different language and not an extra component. Optional Field School 3 and optional Forensic Archaeology listed among practical teaching activities are not silently counted as compulsory. The OER curriculum table rather than illustrative admissions text establishes the credit accounting.
components: Cultural history of the Ancient World 1
Cultural history of the Ancient World 2
Archaeology of Prehistoric and Roman Europe
Archaeology of Medieval Europe and the Early Modern World
Past and Present: Critical approaches to Antiquity and Archaeological Heritage
Dutch-language thesis track; the English-track Bachelor Thesis Archaeology is its alternative, not an additional 12 EC.
Genuinely free 30-EC third-year academic profiling space, subject to approval and level rules.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized source registration is B Archeologie with teaching language Dutch. The adopted 2026–27 OER formally distinguishes the Dutch-language Archeologie trajectory from English-language Archaeology; the Dutch trajectory and its 12-EC Bachelorscriptie Archeologie are selected.

alternatives.label: Archaeology, ancient societies & material culture
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response studies past societies through world and Greek archaeology, material and visual culture, ancient texts, empires, landscapes, heritage and historical research. Earth observation, soils and data courses contribute bounded landscape and evidence methods, but the programme remains a related-fields route without excavation training, archaeometry or an archaeology thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is led by three archaeology courses and a broader sequence in ancient societies, material and visual culture, landscapes, heritage and historical research. The label names that related-fields composition without claiming a full Archaeology bachelor.
progression: Sustainability, philosophy and imperial history foundations precede archaeology, material-culture, landscape and digital methods. ENSGATE101 precedes Earth Observation, the only formal prerequisite within the programme. Introductory archaeology, art history, literature and data work precede advanced heritage, museum, media and research courses. All courses occur in their exact planned terms; seven are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Cultural heritage, museums & public memory
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different heritage route centred on how societies preserve, contest and communicate material culture. It combines archaeology and art history with museums, restitution, public memory, sociology, ethics, rhetoric, documentary practice and humanities research rather than trying to reproduce field archaeology.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum concentrates on museums, heritage ethics, public memory, restitution, community interpretation and documentary communication. The label reflects that institutional and public-facing emphasis.
progression: Foundations in art history, modern history and rhetoric precede archaeology, stylistics, museums and social analysis. Qualitative research, ethics and community communication lead into advanced heritage, public storytelling, persuasion, documentary and humanities research. No selected course has an unmet formal prerequisite, every course occurs in its assigned planned term, and eight courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The heritage route replaces seven courses in environmental science, GIS, soils, data science, ancient literature, philosophy and warfare with seven courses in rhetoric, sociology, qualitative inquiry and ethics. Each programme therefore contains 52.5 EC not present in the other; the substitutions follow from the second route’s public-institutional organising question.

core: Archaeological and material evidence for understanding past societies
Excavation, scientific material analysis and digital archaeological methods
Mediterranean and European societies from prehistory to the early modern period
Archaeological heritage, museums, management and public interpretation
Historical landscapes, cities and human–environment relations
Source criticism, archaeological theory, research and publication
adjacent: Ancient societies through archaeology, history, texts and material culture
Cultural heritage, museums and public memory
Professional field archaeology and archaeometric investigation
questions: What can objects and material remains reveal about past people and societies?
How should archaeological heritage be interpreted, managed and communicated today?
How did people interact with historical landscapes and cities?

candidates.label: Excavation, archaeological science & field investigation
candidates.assessment: UCR has no excavation sequence, stratigraphy, finds processing, archaeological materials laboratory, archaeometry or supervised field school. General GIS, soils, laboratory and data courses cannot be relabelled as archaeological field or scientific training.

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible. The first studies ancient societies and material culture through UCR’s archaeology, history, art, landscape and research courses; the second is a distinct public-heritage and museum route. The next generator-backed direction—excavation, archaeological science and field investigation—cannot be implemented at UCR, so production stops at two and states the disciplinary gap explicitly.

notes.text: VU Archaeology provides a cumulative disciplinary curriculum in archaeological periods, sources, scientific and digital methods, two field schools, material analysis, theory and an archaeology thesis. UCR can build coherent related programmes around ancient societies and material culture or heritage, museums and public memory, but neither is a full Archaeology bachelor.

UCR offers three archaeology/ancient-heritage courses but no excavation sequence, stratigraphy, archaeometry or archaeological-materials laboratory, systematic prehistoric-to-medieval European sequence, supervised field school or archaeology thesis. Environmental fieldwork, GIS and data science remain bounded complementary methods rather than substitutes.
